biography.plain_text: Sir Douglas Myers was a New Zealand brewing magnate who bought out his family's interests in Campbell & Ehrenfried and built Lion Nathan into a major trans-Tasman group. He chaired the New Zealand Business Roundtable during its campaign for market reforms, sold his brewing stake to Kirin and subsequently settled in London.

long_biography.plain_text:
In 1981, brewer Sir Douglas Myers borrowed heavily to buy into Lion while the price of his stake in a separate drinks business remained unsettled. He counted on the eventual payment to cover the borrowing. The gamble succeeded, and he became Lion's managing director, selling peripheral activities and concentrating on brewery efficiency.

His son Campbell's interest in music prompted Myers to invest in Downtown, the New York business that developed into a global music publisher. Its catalogue included administration rights to John Lennon's solo work. Myers also committed capital to Chiltern, supporting the expansion of its clinical-trials business through investment in staff, technology and acquisitions.
